title: U.S. House · Massachusetts's 6th District
area: Massachusetts's North Shore and Merrimack Valley, including Salem, Lynn, Andover, Haverhill and Newburyport.

context.text: Open seat: incumbent Seth Moulton ran for the U.S. Senate in Massachusetts in 2026 rather than seeking re-election, making this the state's most contested House race this cycle (seven candidates filed). Dan Koh defeated five other Democrats, including state representative Tram Nguyen, in the September 1, 2026 Democratic primary. Micah Jones ran unopposed for the Republican nomination.

candidates.name: Dan Koh
candidates.ballotNote: Won the September 1, 2026 Democratic primary with 42.2% of the vote in a six-way field.

summary.text: Dan Koh is the Democratic nominee for the open Massachusetts 6th District seat. He worked as chief of staff to Boston Mayor Marty Walsh, ran unsuccessfully for Congress in 2018, served on the Andover Select Board, and then worked in the Biden administration as chief of staff to Labor Secretary Walsh and later as a White House deputy cabinet secretary and Intergovernmental Affairs deputy director. His campaign website describes a campaign focused on affordability and opposition to President Trump.

background.text: Born in Andover, Massachusetts; according to Wikipedia he was born in 1985, the son of physicians Howard Koh and Claudia Arrigg, and attended Phillips Academy.
Earned a bachelor's degree from Harvard College and an M.B.A. from Harvard Business School.
Interned for Sen. Ted Kennedy for three summers and held a one-year fellowship advising Boston Mayor Thomas Menino, arranged through Harvard Business School.
Served as chief of staff to Arianna Huffington at the Huffington Post, then as chief of staff to Boston Mayor Martin J. Walsh for more than three years, leaving in September 2017.
Ran in the 2018 Democratic primary for Massachusetts's 3rd District and lost to Lori Trahan by 145 votes (18,580 to 18,435) after a recount.
Elected to the Andover Board of Selectmen (now Select Board) in 2019, receiving the most votes of any candidate, and resigned in February 2021 to join the Biden administration.

In 2021 became chief of staff to U.S. Labor Secretary Marty Walsh, then served as Special Assistant to the President and Deputy Cabinet Secretary, ending as Deputy Assistant to the President and deputy director of the White House Office of Intergovernmental Affairs.

As of July 2026, hosted The People's Cabinet podcast. Announced his candidacy in October 2025 after Rep. Seth Moulton ran for the U.S. Senate, and won the September 2026 Democratic primary in a six-candidate field with 42.2% of the vote.

priorities.text: Protecting democracy and standing up to Donald Trump.
Fighting for working families, including affordable housing, healthcare and stronger unions and workers' rights.
Combating climate change and protecting reproductive freedom and LGBTQ+ rights.

positions.summary: Lists protecting reproductive freedom among his priorities for Congress.
Says he will fight climate change in Congress, listing it among his top priorities.
Names making healthcare affordable and accessible as one of his priorities.
positions.quote: My priorities include making healthcare affordable and accessible, addressing the housing crisis, strengthening unions and workers' rights, combating climate change, protecting reproductive freedom, advancing racial justice, defending LGBTQ+ rights, improving public education, reducing gun violence, and investing in transportation infrastructure.

positions.summary: Lists addressing the housing crisis among his stated policy priorities.
Lists reducing gun violence among his stated policy priorities.

candidates.name: Micah Jones
candidates.ballotNote: Ran unopposed for the Republican nomination, winning 99.2% of the September 1, 2026 primary vote.

summary.text: Micah Jones is the Republican nominee for the open Massachusetts 6th District seat. An Army veteran who served with the 82nd Airborne Division, including in Afghanistan, he is an attorney who has represented clients before the SEC. A former Democrat who became an independent and then a Republican, he describes himself as center-right on fiscal issues and says his campaign is built on three priorities: accountability, opportunity and security.

background.text: Served in the U.S. Army from 2011 to 2016, predominantly with the 82nd Airborne Division, including a deployment to Afghanistan from 2014 to 2015.
Earned a bachelor's degree from the University of California, San Diego, and a law degree from Northeastern University School of Law, which he says he paid for using the GI Bill.

Works as an attorney representing clients before the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission, including in SEC investigations and litigation; says this role barred him from trading individual stocks and that members of Congress should be held to the same standard.
Describes himself as a former Democrat; he told Fox News he left the party around 2016, during law school, and became an independent before joining the Republican Party.

In the 2026 race he says the district's seat is open for the first time in 47 years and that he would seek to work with the administration where appropriate; he describes himself as a husband and father.

priorities.text: "Leadership through service": says elected officials should lead by example and focus on delivering results rather than partisan dysfunction.

More opportunity for the North Shore and Merrimack Valley: reducing barriers to business growth, supporting small businesses, making childcare more affordable, and expanding clean and reliable energy.

positions.summary: Says he supports expanding clean and reliable energy alongside continued investment, without committing to a faster transition away from fossil fuels.
positions.quote: That means eliminating unnecessary barriers to economic growth, supporting small businesses, making childcare more affordable, encouraging common sense innovation in areas like artificial intelligence and advanced manufacturing, expanding clean and reliable energy, and creating more pathways for young Americans to serve their communities and develop valuable career skills.
